\section{Discussion}
\label{sec:discussion}

\subsection{Why Logit Baselines Fail the Specificity Test}

The final-layer logit gap measures the difference between the probability of the top refusal token and the top compliance token at the last prompt position. Any perturbation that shifts these probabilities, even by a small amount that does not change the greedy decode, produces a nonzero $\Delta$BL1. Quantisation and dtype casts change the numerical precision of the logit computation, system-prompt swaps change the input distribution, and head-only unembedding edits change the projection matrix. All of these move BL1 without moving behaviour because BL1 operates at the decision boundary while behaviour depends on the argmax.

Activation readouts, by contrast, measure the geometry of the representation space at mid-depth layers, which is more stable under these perturbations. The diff-in-means direction at layer 14 of Qwen3-0.6B is bitwise identical between the bf16 reference and the fp16 cast (the activations are computed in bf16 regardless of storage precision), and the int8 weight-only round-trip changes activations by less than $10^{-3}$ in norm.

\subsection{Decodable but Inert: Implications for Safety Monitoring}

The finding that the refusal direction is decodable at the prompt site but removing it does not change judged refusal has two implications. First, keyword-based refusal detection is unreliable. The keyword proxy reports a 64-percentage-point drop in refusal under site-local F removal, but this reflects a change in phrasing, not in policy. An evaluation that counts ``I cannot'' as refusal and ``This is illegal and I cannot assist'' as compliance will overestimate the effectiveness of interventions. Second, the model's refusal policy is implemented redundantly. Even after the dominant linear direction is removed at one site, the model recovers its refusal through alternative representations or later layers. Global removal of F at all positions and all layers does reduce judged refusal (instruct drops to 0.67), confirming that the direction carries causal information in aggregate, but no single site is sufficient.

This finding extends Galeone et al.'s detection-control dissociation \cite{Galeone2026} from the cross-model setting (where different models show different steerability) to the within-model setting (where different sites within the same model show different causal strength).

\subsection{Limitations}
\label{sec:limitations}

\textbf{Scale.} The specificity audit uses three families at 0.6--1.7B parameters. Larger models may have different false-alarm profiles, and the 15 no-ops, while spanning a range of deployment-relevant modifications, do not cover every possible perturbation.

\textbf{Sensitivity gap.} The activation readouts detect 3--6 of 9 effective changes compared to 5--6 for BL1. Whether this gap closes at larger panel sizes is an open question that the pre-registered confirmation panel (at least 30 new checkpoints from at least 8 new families) is designed to answer.

\textbf{Single architecture for the causal grid.} The causal experiment uses only Qwen3-4B variants. The decodable-but-inert finding may not hold for architectures with different attention patterns 
</pasted_content id="c1c0">


<pasted_content id="c1c0">
or layer counts.

\textbf{Judge limitations.} All behavioural outcomes depend on an LLM judge. The judge achieves high agreement with human labels on a calibration set, but systematic biases (e.g., toward labelling longer responses as compliant) cannot be ruled out.

\textbf{No surviving candidate.} No readout passes the full pre-registered selection rule, because the required gap of 1.0 null-SD below BL1's median no-op displacement is unattainable: the activation readouts' median displacement is already near zero, and BL1's is only moderately above zero. The pre-registered bar was set before the magnitude of BL1's false-alarm rate was known.


\section{Conclusion}
\label{sec:conclusion}

We audited activation-based safety readouts for two properties that a replacement for behavioural benchmarks must have: specificity (no false alarms on no-ops) and causal relevance (the direction matters for behaviour, not just for a probe). Activation readouts at mid-layer depth pass the specificity test with at most 1/15 false alarms, while the final-layer logit gap fails it with 6--8/15. The causal grid reveals that the refusal direction is decodable at every prompt-site cell but removing it changes the first token without changing judged refusal. This dissociation between the keyword proxy and actual safety behaviour that calls for judge-based evaluation in future intervention studies. The single causal lever is over-refusal under the benign-side direction, and SafeRL provides deeper redundancy than standard instruction tuning. These findings establish the false-alarm audit as a necessary validation step for any activation-based safety metric and identify the decodable-but-inert phenomenon as a constraint on site-local causal claims.

    return f"{x:.3f}" if isinstance(x,(int,float)) else str(x)
def fmtci(c):
    if c is None: return "None"
    return f"[{fmt(c[0])},{fmt(c[1])}]"
print(f"{'pair_id':45s} {'family':10s} {'recipe':12s} {'class':14s} {'dHC':>8s} {'dHC_CI':>20s} {'dOR':>8s} {'dOR_CI':>20s}")
for p in pairs:
    pr = p.get("primary", {})
    dhc = pr.get("dHC"); dhc_ci = pr.get("dHC_ci"); dor = pr.get("dOR"); dor_ci = pr.get("dOR_ci")
    fam = p.get("family","?")
    child = p.get("child","")
    recipe = child.split("__")[-1] if "__" in child else p.get("kind","?")
    print(f"{p['pair_id']:45s} {fam:10s} {recipe:12s} {p['observed_class']:14s} {fmt(dhc):>8s} {fmtci(dhc_ci):>20s} {fmt(dor):>8s} {fmtci(dor_ci):>20s}")
print()
print("keys not having family:", [p['pair_id'] for p in pairs if 'family' not in p])
EOF

**(a) Redundancy / distributed reps / backup / self-repair / hydra effect** — **not mentioned anywhere in this handbook.** Zero hits in `SKILL.md`, `volatile.md`, or `SOURCES.md` for "self-repair", "hydra", "redundan*", "backup". This is genuinely map-silent, not "closed" and not "open." The handbook is explicit about what silence means:

> "Map-silence means *not-yet-checked*, NOT *open*. Before committing to any direction this map does not explicitly flag as crowded, run a fresh, dated saturation search and confirm the space is actually unoccupied. … the measured base rate for unchecked lanes in this forge is 11/11 occupied."

So: **"redundancy/self-repair as a PER-CHECKPOINT scalar" is listed nowhere, open or closed.** Given the 11/11 base rate on unchecked lanes, treat it as *probably occupied until you run a live search* — do not treat handbook silence as green light.

**(b) Steering-vector reliability diagnostics** — explicitly **CROWDED**:
> "Activation steering and its reliability diagnostics. Per-sample unreliability and the linear-approximation limit are characterized [S20]; the AxBench verdict already has a published rebuttal [S25]."
S20 verbatim: "steering effect sizes vary across samples and are unreliable for many target behaviors" and "steering vectors are unreliable when the latent target behavior representation is not effectively approximated by the linear steering direction." This matters because several of your candidates (W1, W3, W4, G3) are functionally steering/ablation reliability diagnostics dressed as second-order metrics.

**(c) Model diffing / checkpoint comparison** — addressed only for the crosscoder case, and it's a warning, not an endorsement:
> "the crosscoder L1 loss 'can misattribute concepts as unique to the fine-tuned model, when they really exist in both models'; the same paper ships the BatchTopK fix [S34]."
Adjacent crowded lane: "Developmental / training-dynamics interpretability. Feature evolution is already tracked across pre-training snapshots with crosscoders [S28]," and "Mechanistic interpretability of RL-trained reasoning models … temporal sparse autoencoders already track feature dynamics across RLVR training [S29]." Your four checkpoints (Base/Instruct/SafeRL/abliterated) aren't training snapshots, but a reviewer will ask you to distinguish your cross-variant comparison from this occupied territory.

**(d) Probing-vs-causality / knowledge-action gap** — the handbook's **single strongest, most load-bearing result**, and it cuts directly against your project:
> "Linear probes discriminated hazardous from benign cases with 98.2% AUROC, yet the model's output sensitivity was only 45.1%, a 53-percentage-point knowledge-action gap." SAE feature steering "produced zero effect despite 3,695 significant features," and steering was "indistinguishable from random perturbation" [S3].
Caveat attached by the handbook itself: "The actionability negative result [S3] is one clinical domain, one model family… generalization beyond triage vignettes is unverified." So it's a strong existence proof of the gap, not a general rate — but any of your metrics that infer causal "use" from internal geometry (G3, G4, W1) must show output-level effect, not just decodability, or they fall into this exact trap.

## 2. METHODOLOGY NORMS (binding)

- **Distributions, not point estimates:** "Report a circuit from one seed/hyperparameter/input set" is flagged as the naive move; the fix is to "sample across seeds, hyperparameters and input distributions; report the distribution and stability metrics, not the modal circuit" [S4]. Same for steering: "Claim a steering result from a mean effect at one coefficient" → "give the per-sample distribution and the behaviors where it fails" [S20]. This binds your W1–W4/G1–G4 reporting: single-checkpoint, single-prompt-set point estimates will not clear the bar.
- **Random/matched control is mandatory for actionability claims:** "measure output-level correction AND collateral disruption of already-correct cases, against a random-perturbation control" [S3]. Your W1's "matched-norm orthogonalised random direction" control is the right shape of control per this norm — keep it and also report collateral disruption on unrelated (non-refusal) behavior, not just the target readout.
- **Structural difference ≠ functional/mechanistic difference:** "Read structural difference between two circuits as two mechanisms" → "run edge-level evaluation and cross-condition transfer; source-level evaluation inflates apparent faithfulness" [S23]. This binds W2 (redundancy depth) and G2 (cluster margin): a joint-ablation threshold crossing must be validated by cross-condition transfer (different prompt sets), not one dataset.
- **Attribution-style local measurement has a known bias:** "the dominant error stems from the non-linearities in the downstream network rather than local curvature at the patched component" [S19] — directly relevant to G3 (cosine between fitted axis and the residual delta the band's layers actually add) and W1 (site-local write gain), since both assume a roughly-linear local effect.
- **Causal/alignment claims need a declared, fixed map:** "fix and declare the map class, and make the encoding assumption explicit — unconstrained maps hit 100% interchange-intervention accuracy on randomly initialized models" [S5]. Your "fitted request axis" is an alignment map between an algorithmic direction and model activations — the fitting procedure must be fixed/declared before causal claims (W8 self-lesion cosine, G3) or the result is uninterpretable by this standard.
- **What counts as a valid causal claim, field-wide:** "specific falsifiable hypotheses, and how the evidence provided does and does not support them," or "clear practical benefits over well-implemented baselines" [S14]. A metric that only "improves a proxy metric on one task" is explicitly named as the punished move in the taste table.
- **Gaps I did not find covered at all** (checked explicitly by grep): mean-ablation vs zero-ablation vs resampling-ablation choice, and off-distribution activation artefacts from ablation. The handbook says nothing about these — do not cite it as having a position either way; this is an area to justify from first principles or outside literature, not from this handbook.
- **Gold-standard baseline:** "Activation patching = the gold-standard causal metric; attribution patching = its first-order, gradient-based approximation, adopted for cost [S19]." Any of your W-series claiming causal displacement should be validated against activation patching, not attribution-patching alone.

## 3. SELF-REPAIR specifically

**Nothing.** No paper, name, or magnitude for self-repair, backup heads, or the hydra effect appears anywhere in `SKILL.md`, `volatile.md`, or `SOURCES.md` (confirmed by direct grep, zero matches). This is a genuine blind spot in the handbook relative to your candidate W4 ("self-repair coefficient: fraction of an ablated component that later layers write back") — the handbook gives you no anchor, positive or negative, for this literature. Per the standing directive, treat this as **unchecked, likely-occupied-until-proven-otherwise** (11/11 base rate), and run a fresh dated search before committing W4/W2 as novel.

## 4. DEAD ENDS your candidates might walk into

- **W1, W3, W4, G3** risk re-treading the **crowded "activation steering and its reliability diagnostics"** lane [S20]/[S25] if framed as "how reliable is the direction," rather than the stated novel angle of "how the direction is used" — the distinction needs to be explicit and defensible in the paper, since the handbook's crowded-list entry doesn't distinguish magnitude-reliability from usage-second-order questions.
- **G3** (cosine between fitted axis and the residual delta layers actually add) walks straight into the **attribution-patching non-linearity trap**: "the dominant error stems from the non-linearities in the downstream network rather than local curvature at the patched component" [S19] — a purely linear/local read of "what the layers add" is exactly the diagnosed failure mode.
- **W8** (cosine of fitted axis before/after self-lesion) is a causal-abstraction/alignment-map claim in disguise; without a fixed, declared fitting procedure it risks the vacuity trap: "any neural network can be mapped to any algorithm" under unrestricted alignment maps [S5].
- **W2/G2** (joint-ablation threshold, three-cluster margin) risk the **phantom-specialization** trap — apparent structural differences (redundancy depth differing across checkpoints) "do not correspond to functional differences" unless validated with edge-level + cross-condition transfer [S23].
- **The whole per-checkpoint-scalar framing** is adjacent to two already-crowded lanes — training-dynamics/crosscoder tracking across checkpoints [S28] and temporal SAEs across RLVR training [S29] — and to the model-diffing artefact warning [S34]. A reviewer versed in this handbook will ask why your four-way (Base/Instruct/SafeRL/abliterated) comparison isn't just model diffing with the crosscoder-style misattribution risk, even though you're not using crosscoders.
- **Any claim that a high W/G value causally "explains" refusal behavior** risks the knowledge-action gap: decodable/geometric signal (probe-like) does not imply output-level control — S3's "indistinguishable from random perturbation" is the standing negative result to preempt, not just cite.

## 5. EVALUATION NORMS for a new per-checkpoint interpretability metric

- Must clear the venue's **two-track bar**: "specific falsifiable hypotheses, and how the evidence provided does and does not support them," or "clear practical benefits over well-implemented baselines" [S14] — a new metric that only "improves a proxy metric on one task" is the explicitly punished move in the taste table.
- Must be benchmarked against **established causal-localization baselines**, per the decision guide: "an interpretable variable inside a hidden vector → causal variable localization (supervised DAS leads; SAE features do not beat neurons) [S10]." A reviewer will ask why W1/G3 beat or complement DAS/activation-patching rather than reinventing a weaker proxy.
- Must report **stability across seeds/hyperparameters/prompt draws**, not a modal/point value [S4], and **per-sample distributions** for any steering-shaped effect [S20].
- Must include a **matched random-direction/random-perturbation control** and report **collateral disruption**, not just the target effect [S3].
- Must **declare the alignment/fitting procedure** for the "fitted request axis" as a fixed map before making causal or cross-checkpoint comparability claims [S5].
- Should weight its own evidentiary base honestly: "most 2026 frontier results here are unreviewed preprints; the peer-reviewed anchors are [S5] (NeurIPS 2025 Spotlight), [S10] (ICML 2025), [S22] (BlackboxNLP 2025)" — a reviewer trained on this field will discount claims resting only on unreviewed preprint support, and will want your own metric's validity argued the same way (falsifiable hypothesis + explicit evidence for/against), not asserted by proxy-score improvement alone.

**Bottom line for planning:** the handbook actively supports framing your project around the knowledge-action gap [S3] and gives binding reporting norms (distributions, matched controls, declared alignment maps) that your current candidate list mostly already satisfies in spirit (W1's matched-norm random control is exactly right). Its one dangerous gap is self-repair/redundancy: the handbook has no position on it at all, so before finalizing W2/W4 as the paper's headline novelty, run a live literature search — do not rely on handbook silence as evidence of open space.

In instruct it moves -2.9 nats, and refusal-onset probability at token 1 drops from about 78% to about 4%. Judged refusal of harmful requests stays at 0.92 → 0.88 in instruct and 0.98 in SafeRL: 0 of 18 site×band cells are CAUSAL in either model, because the model rewrites the opening and still refuses.\n- **Local removal fails because refusal is redundant across positions.** In the exploratory T3 control, removing the same F at *every* position within B4 drops instruct refusal to 0.67 (effect_FR -0.33 [-0.48, -0.21]), so the direction is causal. SafeRL's refusal is more robust to that global ablation (exploratory DiD +0.23 [+0.08, +0.38]).\n- **Over-refusal is the site-local lever.** On hard-benign probes, F or N6 removal at mid-depth (B4-B5, at P and D′, and even at E) lowers over-refusal by 0.12-0.19 in both models. Only instruct N6 @ P_B5 survives Holm over 18 cells.\n- **Decodable ≠ causal.** F is decodable in 12 of 18 cells per model, yet 12 of 12 are behaviourally inert for refusal. BL1, RD, T1ref and N1 readouts swing by several nats under interventions that leave behaviour unchanged. The matched random control alone moves BL1 by about 2 nats.\n- **Three checkpoints in activation space.** SafeRL keeps instruct's request and twin axes (cos ≥ 0.84 per band). In abliterated, removing its own F *raises* refusal-onset mass (sign reversal).\n\n## Design\n\n| component | definition |\n|---|---|\n| models | instruct and SafeRL: the full grid. abliterated: the site-P grid, judged site-P generation, readouts, forward-only windows, and the site-E late readout. Each model runs alone on the GPU in bf16 (NVIDIA L4). |\n| depth bands | B1…B6 = sixths of the 36 decoder layers: L0-5, 6-11, 12-17, 18-23, 24-29, 30-35. \"Layer *l*\" is the output of decoder block *l* = hidden index *l*+1. |\n| sites | **P**: the last prompt position only. **D′**: the last prompt position plus decode calls t=1…7, so it can change token 1. **E**: decode calls t=5…20, so tokens 1-5 cannot change by construction. **D**: decode calls 1…8, run only as a readout site, in the teacher-forced windows. |\n| directions | **F**: the model's own request axis per layer, unit(mean EASY-harmful − mean EASY-benign) over the iteration-2 last-prompt-token harvest (`A_prompt.npy`). It uses zero forwards. **N6**: the benign-side XSTest twin direction, unit(mean safe twin − mean unsafe twin), over the 85 confirmatory twin pairs from one prompt-only pass. **N6perp**: N6 orthogonalised to F. **F_perpU**: F with its top-8 refusal-token unembedding rows projected out. |\n| arms | **0**: no intervention. **F / N6 / N6perp / F_perpU**: projection-out, h ← h − (h·v)v, in every layer of the band at the site positions, fp32 math cast to bf16. **R**: random control. At P and in the teacher-forced windows it is *matched displacement*, h ← h − c_F·u, where c_F is the coefficient the F row of the same item removes in the same pass, so the R/F displacement ratio is exactly 1. At D′/E it is the plan's own-coefficient form h ← h − (h·F)u. u is a unit Gaussian direction orthogonalised to span{F, N6}. There are 20 draws for forward-only outcomes and 3 for judged outcomes. **POS**: a positive control that replaces the residual with the mean EASY-benign residual (B3, B4 at P). It measures generic disruption and is not a treatment. |\n| outcomes | Judged refusal / harmful compliance / safe engagement on 48 held-out harmful probes, and judged over-refusal on 48 hard-benign probes. The site-P forward-only grid (registered F1) uses a 6-cell family and additionally needs the empirical p over the 20 R draws to be below 0.05. |\n| decodability | Arm-0 AUROC (32+32 held-out items) of the band-mean standardised projection on F at the site's window. DECODABLE if the bootstrap lower CI bound is above 0.60. |\n| readouts under intervention | BL1_easy / BL1_hard (G1 contrast, final logits applied once, never pooled), N1 (Cohen d along the *unintervened* F at l*), N6, N2 (F_perpU) and N7, on the 256 stimuli under each arm. art_research = {
    "type": "research",
    "objective": (
        "Run the fresh, dated saturation search the field-norm requirement demands BEFORE redundancy "
        "or self-repair may be called novel, re-verify that over-refusal-as-the-target-of-an-internal-"
        "readout is still an open cell, and resolve every bibliography and must-not-claim item so the "
        "final paper's positioning cannot be attacked. A closure must land before the experiments are "
        "written up, not after."
    ),
    "approach": (
        "(1) THE SATURATION SEARCH THAT GATES THE NOVELTY CLAIM. Search, dated today, for prior work "
        "that computes as a PER-CHECKPOINT SCALAR any of: representational redundancy or "
        "distributedness of a safety or refusal feature; the number of sites or layers that must be "
        "ablated jointly before a behaviour collapses; a self-repair / backup-behaviour / hydra-effect "
        "coefficient; a positional redundancy ratio; or a rotation-under-self-lesion statistic. Search "
        "both the safety literature and the general mechanistic-interpretability literature, since "
        "self-repair and backup behaviour are established there and W4 must be positioned as a "
        "scalarisation of a known phenomenon rather than its discovery. For each hit, record whether "
        "it is per-checkpoint or per-input, whether it needs a parent or reference model, and whether "
        "it is scored against behaviour. Mark each of W1-W8 OPEN, PARTIAL or CLOSED with the deciding "
        "passage quoted verbatim and re-fetched independently. If any is CLOSED, say so plainly -- "
        "that is the most valuable thing this lane can return, and it is cheaper to learn it now than "
        "in review.\n\n"
        "(2) THE REGISTERED TARGET. Re-verify, from 2026-09-01 onward and including anything newer "
        "than the iteration-4 pass, that NO per-checkpoint internal readout has been scored against "
        "OVER-REFUSAL as its target. The iteration-4 pass found this OPEN everywhere; confirm or "
        "overturn it. Check specifically arXiv:2609.18471 'First Token Matters', Duan 2606.15980, "
        "arXiv:2609.04721, AMS 2608.05578, N-GLARE, RAS/SafeVec, Aligned Probing and Hurtado "
        "2607.01854, and record for each whether it reports no-op or expression-only controls, "
        "over-refusal as an outcome, a logit baseline, a decode-site readout and a causal test.\n\n"
        "(3) THE DIMENSIONALITY QUESTION. Search for any published claim, in either direction, that "
        "cheap single-model safety readouts are effectively one-dimensional, or for any published "
        "factor analysis / effective-rank treatment of a family of internal safety scores. If the P1 "
        "bound is the paper's outcome, this is the work it must be positioned against; if nothing "
        "exists, say so, because the bound then becomes a contribution rather than a failure.\n\n"
        "(4) AMS OPERATIONAL DETAIL, re-pinned: entry point, default concept pairs, depth window "
        "int(0.4L)..int(0.8L), last-position hidden state, raw text with no chat template, 1-D "

        "Spagliardi, since IRT-based cheap safety benchmarking is the closest competing answer to "

        "prune or cite the five uncited entries (Li2023, Spagliardi2026, Wei2023, Wollschlager2025, "

strategy = {
    "title": "Screen how safety is used, not its size",
    "objective": (
        "Establish whether a cheap single-model safety readout has a SECOND usable coordinate. Four "
        "consecutive screens showed that every candidate so far -- Cohen's d at the best layer, the "
        "Fisher cluster ratio, AMS sigma, the final-layer refusal-logit gap -- is one coordinate "
        "measured four ways (pairwise Spearman 0.71-0.79 across 25 checkpoints). Iteration 5 abandons "
        "LEVELS and screens 15 SECOND-ORDER readouts of how a checkpoint's safety representation is "
        "USED: how much displacing it moves the model's own downstream computation, how many sites "
        "must be removed together before it collapses, how much later layers write it back, how it "
        "rotates under the model's own lesion, and how it is oriented relative to the benign-twin "
        "axis. The registered primary target is OVER-REFUSAL, the one outcome no internal readout has "
        "ever been scored against, with harmful compliance and edit-robustness as co-primaries and a "
        "hard non-collinearity pre-screen that drops any candidate correlating above |0.5| with the "
        "logit gap BEFORE any outcome is read. The competing claim is carried as a real candidate: if "
        "every second-order readout also collapses onto the request axis, the contribution is the "
        "BOUND -- a cheap single-model readout has one coordinate, AMS and the logit gap already read "
        "it, and the false-alarm and over-refusal audits say which to prefer. Alongside this, the "
        "commissioned four-way Qwen3-4B activation comparison is restored to first class with the "
        "Base model put back into the intervention grid."
    ),
    "rationale": (
        "DIAGNOSIS. Iteration 4 returned weak_or_null and the hypothesis widened, so this is a WIDE "
        "SCREEN, not another deep test. Two things went wrong and both are fixable by design rather "
        "than by effort. First, the preregistered bar was unattainable by an order of magnitude: it "
        "demanded a median no-op displacement 1.0 null SD below BL1's, but BL1 itself only moves "
        "0.150, so the achieved gap of -0.126 could never have passed. The bar was written before the "
        "incumbent's magnitude was known. Second, and more important, sensitivity rather than "
        "specificity is the binding failure: every activation candidate detects at most 6 of 9 "
        "effective changes and NOT ONE detects AMD-OLMo base to SFT in the registered direction. Two "
        "text bars that cost zero forward passes -- the model-card regex at 0/15 and 5/9, and the "

"""
NEW:  (F) MAP-SILENCE IS NOT OPEN. The handbook contains ZERO mentions of self-repair, hydra effect,
     backup behaviour or redundancy, and it states that map-silence means not-yet-checked, with a
     measured base rate of 11 of 11 unchecked lanes turning out to be occupied. So
     redundancy-as-a-per-checkpoint-scalar and self-repair-as-a-per-checkpoint-coefficient may NOT be
     called novel until the research lane's fresh dated saturation search returns. Plan for the
     search coming back OCCUPIED: W2 and W4 are then reported as measurements positioned against
     that work, and the paper's novelty rests on the over-refusal target and the graded-no-op audit.
 (G) STEERING-RELIABILITY IS A CROWDED LANE and W1, W3, W4 and G3 sit next to it. Per-sample
     unreliability and the linear-approximation limit of steering are already characterised. No
     candidate is presented as a new steering method or as a steering-reliability diagnostic; the
     defensible framing is HOW THE DIRECTION IS USED BY THE MODEL'S OWN DOWNSTREAM COMPUTATION, and
     that distinction must be made explicitly in the text rather than left implicit.
 (H) ACTIVATION PATCHING IS THE GOLD-STANDARD CAUSAL METRIC and the first-order gradient-based
     approximation's dominant error comes from downstream NON-LINEARITY, not local curvature. W1 and
     G3 both assume a roughly linear local effect, so on a declared subset of cells they must be
     validated against a real activation patch, and the agreement or disagreement is reported.
 (I) STRUCTURAL DIFFERENCE IS NOT FUNCTIONAL DIFFERENCE (the phantom-specialisation trap). W2 and G2
     compare structure across checkpoints, so a threshold crossing must be validated by
     CROSS-CONDITION TRANSFER -- a second, disjoint prompt set -- before it is read as a mechanism.
 (J) DECLARE THE ALIGNMENT MAP. The axis-fitting procedure is fixed and written into the prereg
     before any causal or cross-checkpoint claim, because unconstrained maps reach 100% interchange
     accuracy on randomly initialised networks. The random-init arm already on disk is the control
     that shows the fitted map is not vacuous.
 (K) ABLATION TYPE IS A CHOICE THAT MUST BE JUSTIFIED. The handbook takes no position on
     mean-ablation versus zero-ablation versus resampling, or on off-distribution activation
     artefacts, so justify the directional projection-out choice from first principles, report the
     resulting activation norm displacement, and check that intervened activations stay inside the
     model's own distribution rather than assuming it.
 (L) DISTINGUISH THIS FROM MODEL DIFFING. Training-dynamics tracking across checkpoints and
     crosscoder model diffing are occupied lanes, and crosscoder L1 is known to misattribute
     concepts as unique to the fine-tuned model. The four-way comparison here is per-checkpoint
     self-fitted and parent-free by construction, which is exactly the property that avoids that
     artefact, and the paper must say so rather than leave the reviewer to ask.
"""

## 3. `src/`, `src_h2/`, `src_i3/` modules

**`src/`** (current, active pipeline):
- `harvest_variants.py` — harvests all 27 arrays per in-house arm (prompt/C11/AMS/decode-site passes, vmin Gram-least-eigenvector).
- `ams_reimpl.py` — reimplementation of the published AMS scanner (2608.05578): `ams_prompts`, `harvest_ams`, `_direction_and_separation`, `ams_tier1`, `ams_tier2`, `safety_level`.
- `ncands.py` — the 32-candidate scoring engine: axis fitting, N1–N12, BL1, C4/C7/C13, B7, regex, AMS wrappers, k-curve.
- `common.py` — logging/hashing/JSON/device utils, deviation ledger.
- `items.py` — XSTest twin loader.
- `judge.py` — LLM-judge runner + cost ledger.
- `truth_classify.py` — NOOP/EFFECTIVE/OR_EFFECTIVE/AMBIGUOUS rule + paired bootstrap → `results/classification.json`.
- `build_harvested_truth.py`, `build_pairs_to_score.py`, `pairs.py`, `variants.py` — pairing/config generation.
- `gen_variants.py` — generates model checkpoints/variants (in-house arms).
- `device_swap.py`, `hook_check.py`, `score_watch.py`, `validate_ams.py`, `test_scoring.py`, `test_t0.py`, `amend.py`, `make_readme.py`, `prereg.py` — infra/QA/prereg-tracking.
- `assembly/` — `hygiene_check.py`, `merge_view.py`, `order_proof_per_arm.py`, `text_bars.py`, `write_readme.py` (report assembly).

**`src_h2/`** (an earlier harvest/scoring generation, superseded but data-compatible):
- `harvest.py`, `c_harvest2.py` — earlier harvest pass; `panel.py`, `score_panel.py`, `score_ckpt.py` — earlier per-checkpoint scoring; `judge_ext.py`, `judge_ext_lanec.py` — earlier judge; `analyze.py`, `numerics.py`, `wsummary.py`, `randinit_wsummary.py`, `weightfp.py` — stats/fingerprint utils; `t1_tests.py`, `t2_lesion_control.py`, `t7_determinism.py` — unit tests; `fetch_cards.py`, `fetch_models.py` — HF metadata; `leak_audit.py`, `session2_deviations.py`, `split_large_arrays.py`, `sweep.py`, `confirm.py`, `make_outputs.py`, `assets_build.py`, `aii_common.py`.

**`src_i3/`** (iter-3 generation; `src_i3/h2/` nests a copy of `src_h2`):
- `candidates.py` — iter-3 candidate metric definitions (predecessor of `ncands.py`, referenced in `ncands.py`'s docstring "conventions copied from src_i3/candidates.py").
- `extra_analyses.py` — Gram-matrix `PromptModel` speed trick that `ncands.py` reuses.
- `gen.py`, `harvest_panel.py`, `iter2_panel_same_code.py`, `panel.py`, `score.py`, `stats_panel.py`, `outcomes.py`, `judge.py`, `prereg.py`, `items.py`, `c11_items.py`, `hf_probe.py`, `inventory.py`, `b7_diagnostic.py`, `build_struct_out.py`, `time_rule.py`, `unit_checks.py`, `verify_hooks.py`, `test_shrink.py`, `common.py` — iter-3 pipeline stages, largely superseded by `src/`.
- `h2/` subfolder — copy of `src_h2` snapshot used at iter-3 time.

Specific functions requested:
- **(a) request-axis direction F**: `src/ncands.py:153 axis_weight_vector(y, w, mask)` — fits `c = unit(weighted_mean_y1 − weighted_mean_y0)` on the EASY set; used by `src/ncands.py:580 crossfit_lstar(...)` (cross-fit train/test axis) and by every N-candidate via `d_auroc_fisher_curves`.
- **(b) N1/N6**: N1 (`d_l*`) is `src/ncands.py:580 crossfit_lstar(...)` → `l_star, d_cf`. N6 (benign separation) is computed inline in `src/ncands.py:929 values(...)` around line 1005 (`out["N6"] = cohens_d_w(...)` on XSTest harmful-twin vs benign-twin projections at `l_star1`); reused in `k_curve_point` (line 1211).
- **(c) AMS sigma**: `src/ams_reimpl.py:351 ams_tier1(...)` computes per-concept and mean `sigma` (separation), called by `src/ncands.py:904 ams_t1_values(ckpt, w_ams)` which emits `AMS_T1_sigma`.
- **(d) judge**: `src/judge.py:190 judge_file(gf, concurrency)` runs the LLM judge over a generations file; `src/truth_classify.py` consumes its output (`labels`) to build `graded_truth.json`.
- **(e) paired bootstrap**: `src/truth_classify.py:118 paired_boot(lab_p, lab_c, harm, ben, rng)` — B=2000 paired-index bootstrap (same resample indices for parent/child), returns `dHC/dHC_ci, dOR/dOR_ci, dSE/dSE_ci`; classification thresholding in `src/truth_classify.py` `rule(b)` (~line 141).

## 4. Decode-site (generation-time activation) pass

Yes — `src/harvest_variants.py:70 dec_harvest(model, tok, texts, n_new, batch, eos)` runs a **greedy 8-new-token generation pass** on the 160 HARD stimuli and saves per-layer hidden states at the generated positions (`A_dec.npy` = mean-pooled over generated tokens before first EOS; `A_dec_tok1.npy` = first generated token only; `dec_ntok.npy` = tokens generated per row, mean 8.0). Consumed by candidates `N9_decode_d`, `N9_tok1`, `N10_dec_minus_prompt` in `src/ncands.py`.

**Coverage**: every one of the 53 harvest tag dirs (all `F1/F2/F3__*` and all `HG__*`) has `A_dec.npy` + `A_dec_tok1.npy` + `dec_ntok.npy` present with `DONE` markers — i.e. the decode-site pass ran for the full harvest set, not a subset.

# Recon: `gen_art_experiment_2` (iter_4) — causal depth×site grid, Qwen3-4B family

Root: `/ai-inventor/aii_data/runs/run_YqmEFECOIR3D/3_invention_loop/iter_4/gen_art/gen_art_experiment_2`

## 1. `src/engine.py` — intervention mechanics

Hooks are **PyTorch forward hooks on each decoder layer** (`layer.register_forward_hook`), registered once at model load and toggled by an `active`/`None` `Spec` object per call (never re-registered).

Key classes/functions:
- `class Engine.__init__(repo, n_threads=2, device=None)` — loads bf16 model, asserts `generation_config` has no argmax-altering logits processors (so the hand-rolled greedy loop == HF greedy generate).
- `Engine.register_hooks()/remove_hooks()` — one `register_forward_hook` per of the 36 `self.layers`.
- `Engine._make_hook(l)` — the hook closure, keyed by layer index `l`.
- `Engine.build_spec(rows, dirs, readout, bands) -> Spec` — prompt-pass-only intervention spec (site P).
- `Engine.site_generate(pre, rows, sites, dirs, bands, *, max_new, readout)` — builds per-decode-step `Spec`s inside the greedy loop for sites P/D′/E; edits are turned on/off per step via `SITE_WINDOWS = {"P": (True,0,-1), "D": (False,1,8), "Dprime": (True,1,7), "E": (False,5,20)}` (edit-the-last-prompt-token?, first decode call, last decode call).
- `Engine.stacked_pass(pre, rows, spec, *, max_new=0)` — teacher-forced span pass (spanD/spanE), decode continuation optionally hook-inactive.
- `Engine._greedy_continue(...)` — custom greedy loop, drops finished rows from batch+KV cache each step.

Matched-norm displacement / arms, `OWN_ARMS`/`MATCHED_ARMS` (engine.py:95-98):
```python
OWN_ARMS = {"F": ("F", "F"), "N6": ("N6", "N6"), "N6perp": ("N6perp", "N6perp"), "FperpU": ("FperpU", "FperpU"),
            "RFo": ("F", "U"), "RN6o": ("N6", "U"), "RUo": ("FperpU", "U")}
MATCHED_ARMS = {"RF": "F", "RN6": "N6"}
```
Core hook body (`_make_hook`, engine.py:155-192), verbatim excerpt:
```python
h = output[0] if isinstance(output, tuple) else output
S = spec.n_pos
x = h[:, -S:, :].float()                                     # [R, S, d] site positions
op = spec.layer_ops.get(l)
if op is not None:
    c_all = torch.einsum("rsd,rd->rs", x, op["V"])            # measured on each row
    c = c_all[op["src"]] * op["has"][:, None]                 # coefficient from the source row
    dx = c[..., None] * op["W"][:, None, :]
    x = x - dx
    dn = dx.norm(dim=-1)                                      # [R, S]
    if op["patch"] is not None:
        pm = op["patch"]
        tgt = op["target"][None, None, :].expand_as(x)
        dn = torch.where(pm[:, None], (tgt - x).norm(dim=-1), dn)
        x = torch.where(pm[:, None, None], tgt, x)
    spec.disp[l] = (c.detach(), dn.detach())
```
So each own-coefficient arm (F/N6/N6perp/F_perpU) removes `h ← h - (h·v)v` for its own direction `v = op["V"]`, in fp32, cast back to bf16 on write-back. **Matched-norm displacement**: for arm `RF`/`RN6` at prompt-pass-only sites, `op["src"]` points row `r` at the *F-row or N6-row of the same item/band* (`src_of` dict keyed on `(item, band, arm)`), so the coefficient `c` used for the random direction `W` (a draw `u`) is literally the coefficient the matched F/N6 row measured — giving the random control exactly the same displacement norm as the real direction on the same item. At decode-only sites (D′/E), the "own-coefficient" arms `RFo`/`RN6o`/`RUo` instead use `(h·F)` or `(h·N6)` measured on the **same row itself** (cross-row source undefined once trajectories diverge).

Random control `R` draw (engine.py:666-676):
```python
def random_pool(F: np.ndarray, N6: np.ndarray, J: int, model_idx: int, seed: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """u[l, j] = unit Gaussian draw seeded (seed, model, l, j), orthogonalised against span{F_l, N6_l}."""
    L, d = F.shape
    U = np.zeros((L, J, d), np.float32)
    for l in range(L):
        Q, _ = np.linalg.qr(np.stack([F[l], N6[l]], 1).astype(np.float64))
        for j in range(J):
            g = np.random.default_rng([seed % (2**32), model_idx, l, j]).standard_normal(d)
            g = g - Q @ (Q.T @ g)
            U[l, j] = unit_np(g)
    return U
```
20 draws for forward-only outcomes, 3 for judged generation outcomes (README). `POS` arm patches the residual to `dirs["target"][l]` (mean EASY-benign residual) — a positive/disruption control, not a treatment.

Post-cast residual-ratio check (`resid_ratio`) verifies max `|x·v|/|x|` on check rows after bf16 cast, logged into `Spec.resid_ratio`.

## 2. `src/prep.py` — direction sourcing and depth bands

**No model forward passes** in prep.py (STAGE 0, docstring says "no model is loaded here"). `F` is **refit from disk activations**, not loaded pre-computed:
- `disk_directions(tag, stim)` loads `H2/harvest/<tag>/A_prompt.npy` (shape `(256, 37, 2560)`, iter-2 harvest), `WU_ref.npy`, `WU_ctl.npy`, `token_ids.json`, `gamma.npy`.
- `F[l] = unit(mean(A_easy, y=1) - mean(A_easy, y=0))` per layer, on the EASY split of the 256 stimuli (own model, own forward-free fit).
- `l_star = argmax_{l in [4,33]} Cohen's d of F-projection on HARD split`.
- `F_perpU` = F minus its projection onto the top-8 refusal-unembedding-row span.
- Path constants (`common.py`): `H2 = RUN/iter_2/gen_art/gen_art_experiment_1` (harvest source), `D2 = RUN/iter_2/gen_art/gen_art_dataset_1`, `D1 = RUN/iter_1/gen_art/gen_art_dataset_1` (twin pairs), `I1_DIRS = RUN/iter_1/gen_art/gen_art_experiment_1/out/released/directions` (only used for cosine comparisons, not as the F/N6 source).

**N6 is NOT built in prep.py** — grep across `src/*.py` finds N6 only *consumed* in `engine.py`/`analyze.py`; it is computed elsewhere (twin-pair contrast: `unit(mean safe-twin - mean unsafe-twin)` over 85 confirmatory XSTest twin pairs, per README, "over one prompt-only pass" — this happens inside the GPU driver script at runtime, which is **not present in `src/`** — see note below). Outputs of prep.py: `assets/items.json`, `prereg.json`(+sha256), `out/private/directions_disk_<model>.npz` (F, FperpU, mu_easy_benign, l_star, etc. — deleted before release), `results/disk_readouts.json`.

**Depth bands** (`common.py:172`): `BANDS = {f"B{k}": list(range(6*(k-1), 6*k)) for k in range(1,7)}` — i.e. **6 bands × 6 layers each** for the 36-layer model: B1=L0-5, B2=L6-11, B3=L12-17, B4=L18-23, B5=L24-29, B6=L30-35. Convention: "layer *l*" = decoder-block-*l* output = hidden index *l*+1.

**Note for the new experiment**: the actual GPU-grid driver that builds `Row` lists, calls `Engine.site_generate`/`stacked_pass`, and fits N6 at runtime is **not in `src/`** (only `engine.py`, `analyze.py`, `prep.py`, `bench_cpu.py`, `common.py`, `figures.py`, `judge.py`, `peek.py`, `stats.py`, test files exist). It must have been a temporary/inline script invoked from the shell commands behind `logs/main_gpu.out` etc. — the new experiment will need to reconstruct or find that driver logic (build_spec/site_generate call sites) before it can run a grid.

Two-sidedness DiD table (`summary_tables.md` bottom): `ALL: F_refused_harm DiD +0.146 [-0.021,+0.333]`, `B4: +0.229 [+0.083,+0.375]` (largest positive DiD band).

**(d) Direction cosine tables** (`three_model_comparison._cross_model_direction_cosines_by_band`, band-mean):

| pair | B1 | B2 | B3 | B4 | B5 | B6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| cos_F instruct-saferl | 0.997 | 0.982 | 0.916 | 0.895 | 0.901 | 0.841 |
| cos_F instruct-abliterated | 0.999 | 0.994 | 0.943 | **0.412** | **0.306** | **0.328** |
| cos_F saferl-abliterated | 0.996 | 0.976 | 0.875 | **0.319** | **0.251** | **0.252** |
| cos_N6 instruct-saferl | 0.995 | 0.977 | 0.889 | 0.922 | 0.918 | 0.863 |
| cos_N6 instruct-abliterated | 0.997 | 0.926 | 0.609 | **0.021** | **0.027** | **0.061** |
| cos_N6 saferl-abliterated | 0.994 | 0.913 | 0.585 | **0.023** | **0.030** | **0.054** |

Abliterated's F/N6 directions rotate away from instruct/SafeRL from B4 onward (cos ≈0.3-0.4 for F, ≈0.02-0.06 for N6) — exactly the band range where F causally drives token-1 refusal-onset mass in the other two models. `l_star`/`n6_best`: instruct 26/26 (B5), saferl 26/31 (B5/B6), abliterated 23/19 (B4).

## 5. `prior_session_confirm_panel/`

**Not part of this experiment.** Per `README.md:276` and `.aii/manifest.yaml:10`: *"A different plan's session-1 outputs, found in this workspace and moved aside in session 2. They are not part of this experiment."* It is the leftover working tree of a **separate iteration-4 confirmation-panel project** ("Iteration-4 CONFIRMATION panel — blind scoring of N1-N13", `prereg.json`, seed `iter4_confirm_panel_v1`) — matches the `NoOpSet Exec I4` memory entry (in-house NOOP/EFFECTIVE pairs, hash chain, ≥30-checkpoint panel). Contents: `assets/` (behaviour_items, c11_items, cell_char_spans, cells, panel_rule+sha256, prereg_subsets, stimuli, token_sets), `baselines/`, `harvest/RandInit-gemma-3-1b-it_SMOKE/`, `hash_chain.jsonl`, `logs/` (ams_fidelity_check, ams_install, gen, harvest, judge, panel, prereg, venv_install, 322 files total under the dir), `out/released/`, `pyproject.toml`, `results/` (ams_fidelity_check.json, arch_precheck.json, fp16_benchmark.json, gen_timings.json, panel.json+amend+trim, prereg.json, provenance.json, run_list.json, scores_sealed/), `src/` (~25 files: ams_reimpl.py, ams_run.py, candidates.py, gen.py, harvest_confirm.py, harvest_panel.py, panel.py, score.py, stats_confirm.py/panel.py, etc.). It has its own `.venv_ams` python 3.12 environment (`uv sync --project prior_session_confirm_panel`). **Ignore for the new experiment** unless deliberately reusing its confirm-panel machinery.

## 6. `out/cells/` — format and reusability

Structure: `out/cells/{instruct,saferl,abliterated,smoke}/<stage>_<band>__<hook_hash>.{npz,json}` — 148 files for instruct (~30 MB), 30 MB saferl, 21 MB abliterated, 3.4 MB smoke. Each cell = one (model, stage, band) unit, e.g. `genP_B4__6e406f7f.npz` + matching `.json`.

**`.npz` arrays** (per-row, row order defined by the sidecar JSON `rows` list): for judged-generation cells (`genP_*`), arrays are `RD, G1, T1ref, tok1, proj_win [R,4,36,3] fp16, refused, refused_raw, harmful_compliance, safe_engagement, over_refusal, judged, proxy_refused, n_new_tokens` — one float/int per row (R=1056 for B4 e.g.). For simpler cells (`gsm_*`) just `correct, n_new_tokens` (80 rows).

**`.json` sidecar**: `rows` (list of `{item_id, arm, band, draw, site}` dicts — the per-row key that indexes into the `.npz` arrays), plus `kinds, logs, seconds, max_new_tokens, checks, site, band, layers, arms, windows, proj_win_dirs, site_windows, judge_stats, judged_utc`.

**Reusability**: yes — per-item, per-arm, per-band **numeric outcome data is fully preserved and reusable** for re-analysis (that's exactly what `src/analyze.py` consumes to build `results/analysis.json`). **No raw generated text is stored**: `results/judge_label_cache.jsonl` (15,851 rows) is keyed only by `sha256(prompt+response)` → judge label; `out/private/` (where responses would have lived) is empty — deleted before release per `prep.py` docstring ("never released, deleted before submission"). So a new experiment can reuse item/arm/band-level outcome scalars but cannot recover the literal generated text from disk.

## 7. VRAM

No explicit peak-VRAM-allocated metric (`torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated`) is logged anywhere in `logs/`. Only **free-memory-before-load** snapshots and a self-imposed per-process cap are logged, e.g.:
```
CUDA NVIDIA L4: free 23.5 / 23.7 GB; per-process cap 0.55; KV budget 2.5 GB
```
Sequence across sub-runs shows the process releasing memory between stages: `main_gpu.out` starts at 23.5/23.7 GB free; `genG_gpu.out` starts at only 16.7/23.7 GB free (prior process not fully reaped yet); `abliterated_gpu.out` and `genU_e2x2_gpu.out`/`gsm_gpu.out` back to 23.2-23.5/23.7 GB free. `smoke_gpu2.out`/`smoke_gpu3.out` (earlier smoke tests, concurrent contention) saw only 6.5 GB / 8.1 GB free with per-process cap dropped to 0.11 and KV budget 0.3 GB.

**No OOM events found** — `grep -i "OOM\|out of memory\|CUDA out"` across all `logs/*.out` and `logs/*.log` returns nothing. KV-cache footprint is logged per prefill stage instead, e.g. `instruct: eval prefix caches 540 MB; max prompt len 83`, `stimro prefix caches 1312 MB; max prompt len 108` — largest observed prefix-cache footprint was **1312 MB** (stimro, 256 items). Model weights themselves: Qwen3-4B bf16 ≈ 8 GB (4B params × 2 bytes), consistent with the 0.55 per-process cap × 23.7 GB ≈ 13 GB ceiling leaving room for that plus KV cache and activations, but no direct peak-allocated number is recorded in this experiment's logs.

FINAL iteration (5 of 5) strategy for the Qwen3-4B cheap-safety-metric run `run_YqmEFECOIR3D`.
Title: "Screen how safety is used, not its size". 5 artifacts, all parallel.

**Core move.** Levels are abandoned after four collinear nulls (every prior candidate rho 0.71-0.79
with BL1). The screened population is 15 SECOND-ORDER readouts in families that can disagree:
W1-W8 write-handle/redundancy (site-local write gain, redundancy depth, positional redundancy ratio,
self-repair, benign-side gain, signed two-sided gain, decode-site gain, rotation-under-self-lesion);
G1-G4 dimensionless geometry; A1-A3 competing mechanisms carried from the hypothesis alternates
(zero-prompt refusal PRIOR + evidence slope, benign-only footprint, domain-profile dispersion);
P1 the one-coordinate bound, tested by the pre-screen count plus effective rank.
Registered primary target = OVER-REFUSAL. First selection clause = drop any candidate with
|Spearman| >= 0.5 against BL1_easy BEFORE any outcome is read.

**The structural fix that mattered most.** There is no iteration 6, so the confirmation join is built
INSIDE iteration 5: a blind SUBSTRATE artifact grades new checkpoints and saves arrays but computes
no candidate value; the SCREEN artifact freezes a hashed survivor.json before globbing
`iter_5/gen_art/*/results/panel_manifest.json`; the EVALUATION artifact re-runs the join as a
backstop. Two independent hash chains make the ordering checkable.

**Artifacts:** (1) commissioned Qwen3-4B four-way with Base RESTORED to the intervention grid plus
the judged-refusal positive control that iteration 4 lacked; (2) the wide screen + freeze + join;
(3) blind held-out substrate producer; (4) evaluation owning all 11 BLOCKING reviewer must-fixes;
(5) research running the mandatory fresh saturation search on redundancy/self-repair.

**Hard operational facts verified this session, reusable by later work:**
- GPU is an NVIDIA L4, 23,034 MiB, idle. 48 cores, 62 GB cgroup RAM.
- Container ROOT filesystem is only 40 GB; `/ai-inventor/aii_data` is a 2.2 PB network mount.
  HF_HOME MUST be redirected into the workspace or model downloads kill the pod.
- Three concurrent GPU artifacts over-subscribe the card (10.0 + 5.5 + 8.5 = 24 GB), so the strategy
  mandates a flock-guarded VRAM lease file under `iter_5/gpu_lease/` with a 20-minute stale-lease TTL.
- iteration-4 venvs were REAPED; `bash restore.sh [cpu|gpu|ams|all]` must run first.
- iteration-4 harvest has 53 tags x 27 files and 72 graded checkpoint rows (far more than planning
  assumed), and a decode-site pass (`A_dec.npy`, `A_dec_tok1.npy`) already exists for every tag.

**Field-handbook constraint discovered here:** the mech-interp handbook has ZERO mentions of
self-repair, hydra effect, backup behaviour or redundancy, and states map-silence means
not-yet-checked with a base rate of 11/11 unchecked lanes turning out occupied. So W2/W4 novelty is
gated on a live search, and the strategy tells the research lane to plan for OCCUPIED.

### [278] ASSISTANT · 2026-09-21 23:02:17 UTC

```
Strategy written and validated at `.terminal_claude_agent_struct_out.json`: one strategy, five parallel artifacts.

**The strategy: "Screen how safety is used, not its size."** Four straight screens failed because every candidate was a separability *level* on the request axis, correlating 0.71 to 0.79 with the logit gap. So the quantity class changes. Fifteen second-order readouts of how a safety representation is *used* go into a wide screen: site-local write gain, redundancy depth, positional redundancy, self-repair, rotation under the model's own lesion, four dimensionless geometry measures, and three competing mechanisms carried from the hypothesis alternates including a zero-prompt refusal prior. The first selection clause drops any candidate correlating above 0.5 with the logit gap before any outcome is read. Registered primary target is over-refusal, the one cell prior art leaves open.

**The structural problem I had to solve.** This is the last iteration, artifacts cannot consume each other, and there is no iteration 6 to run the confirmation join. So the join is built inside the iteration: a blind producer artifact grades new checkpoints and saves arrays but computes no candidate value, the screen artifact freezes a hashed survivor list before globbing the producer's manifest, and the evaluation artifact re-runs the join as a backstop. Two independent hash chains make the ordering checkable rather than asserted.

Five artifacts:

1. **Qwen3-4B four-way, restored to first class.** Base, instruct, SafeRL, abliterated, plus the non-safety fine-tune control, with Base put back into the intervention grid and the judged-refusal positive control the reviewer demanded.
2. **The wide screen**, plus the pre-screen, the effective-rank test of the competing one-coordinate claim, and the join.
3. **The blind held-out substrate producer**: 20 new checkpoints from 6 never-loaded families, a fresh no-op set where every no-op can move both readout classes, and the sealed 54-scenario split.
4. **Evaluation** owning all eleven blocking reviewer must-fixes with re-derived numbers.
5. **Research** running the saturation search that gates the redundancy and self-repair novelty claims.

Four facts from reconnaissance changed the plan rather than decorating it. The iteration-4 virtual environments were reaped, so `restore.sh` runs first. The container root filesystem is 40 GB while the data mount is petabyte-scale, so the model cache must be redirected or the pod dies. The executed grid needed about 13 GB of video memory, not the 10 I had budgeted, which forced a lease protocol across the three GPU artifacts on one 23 GB card. And the grid driver that called the intervention engine is missing from the saved source tree, which is a day of work if an executor discovers it late.

One deliberate deviation from the hypothesis text: its sensitivity bar of seven of nine effective pairs including the case every activation readout currently misses would repeat iteration 4's unattainable-bar failure. I split survival into two tiers so the rule can resolve, and every column still prints.
```
